caustica.options.rt.advancedGrading.tool: Off - the default - uses the authored look: the look package's scene-referred LMT followed by the ACES 2.0 display transform, which is also where the Look Transform control applies. On replaces both with the built-in AgX grading, which holds saturated colors vivid as highlights roll off and uses its own exposure and saturation sliders instead.
caustica.options.rt.exposureMode.tooltip: How the ray-traced image is mapped to display brightness. Auto adapts to scene luminance; Manual uses the exposure value directly.
caustica.options.rt.manualEv.tooltip: Exposure compensation in stops. In Manual, this is the fixed exposure. In Auto, this biases the auto exposure brighter or darker.
caustica.options.rt.nightLift.tooltip: How far night is moved off where auto exposure would place it, in stops. Negative is darker, positive is brighter, and 0.00 is the authored night. It follows how dark the sky is rather than how bright the frame looks, so a night scene holding a lantern or a lit window moves with it, and midday is untouched. Auto exposure sets one level for the whole image, so this darkens or brightens everything in the frame together, lamps included.
caustica.options.rt.gamma.tooltip: Final luminance gamma. Values below 1.00 brighten shadows and midtones while preserving black, white, and color ratios.
caustica.options.rt.purkinje.tooltip: How the eye reads color in dim light: as it adapts to darkness, sensitivity moves away from red, so red flowers, brick and torchlight fall toward black while blue, cyan and green keep their brightness. Nothing happens while the scene is bright - it starts only below roughly 5 nits of absolute scene brightness and is complete by 0.005 nits, so full daylight and dusk look exactly as they did. Needs Auto Exposure: it adapts to how bright the world actually is, not to how bright the frame was made to look.
caustica.options.rt.purkinjeStrength.too: How far the shift goes. 1.00 is the standard night-vision response; lower keeps reds readable at night, higher collapses them sooner. Mid-grey keeps its exact brightness at any value, so this changes which colors win in the dark without changing how bright the dark is.
caustica.options.rt.look.tooltip: Apply the look package's scene-referred LMT, with Advanced Color Grading off. Turn off to see the exposed image straight through ACES 2.0 - useful when telling whether a flat or lifted image comes from the look or from the lighting.
caustica.options.rt.agxExposure.tooltip: Brightness of the AgX grading, which anchors middle grey at a fixed level independent of the exposure above. Raise it with Advanced Color Grading on if the image reads dark at the same Exposure EV.
caustica.options.rt.agxSaturation.toolti: Color intensity of the AgX grading, around the image's own brightness. AgX compresses chroma hard as highlights roll off, so values above 1.00 restore the vividness that costs it. 1.00 is neutral.
caustica.options.rt.risCandidates.toolti: Candidates each surface tests when picking a glowing block to sample. Higher is less noisy on torch and lava light but costs more. Off falls back to lighting from emitters only when a ray hits one.
caustica.options.rt.spp.tooltip: Path-tracing samples taken per pixel each frame. Higher is cleaner but more demanding.
caustica.options.rt.maxBounces.tooltip: Maximum number of secondary path-tracing bounces after the primary hit. Higher captures more indirect light but costs more.
caustica.options.rt.entities.tooltip: Include entities and block entities in the ray-traced scene.
caustica.options.rt.traceSelf.tooltip: Show your own body in reflections, shadows and indirect light while in first person (you see yourself in water as others see you). Turn off to exclude your body from every ray; third person and other players are unaffected.
caustica.options.rt.particles.tooltip: Draw particles as camera-ray billboards inside the traced scene.
caustica.options.rt.glow.tooltip: Draw the vanilla Glowing-effect outline (through walls) around glowing entities.
caustica.options.rt.waterWaves.tooltip: Animate water-surface normals for moving wave highlights.
caustica.options.rt.vanillaSun.tooltip: Draw the sun from the sun sprite, so a resource pack's own art shows. Off draws it as a circular disc instead, at the same angular size the sunlight is sampled at, which makes its apparent size and the softness of its shadows agree.
caustica.options.rt.vanillaMoon.tooltip: Draw the moon from the phase sprite, so a resource pack's own art shows. Off draws a sphere lit by the sun's actual direction, so the terminator points the right way for the time of night and the surface keeps its maria.
caustica.options.rt.waterWaveHeight.tool: How tall the waves are, as a percent of the default look (100%). Taller waves break up reflections more and focus underwater caustics more sharply; 0% leaves the surface a flat mirror.
caustica.options.rt.waterWaveSize.toolti: Wavelength as a percent of the default look (100%). The whole spectrum scales together, so low values are pond ripples and high values are long ocean swell.
caustica.options.rt.waterWaveSpeed.toolt: How fast the waves travel, as a percent of the default look (100%). Long swell still moves faster than short chop at any setting; 0% freezes the surface.
caustica.options.rt.waterReflection.tool: How much of its mirror-like sky reflection the water surface keeps. At 100% water is a perfect dielectric and reproduces the bright band of sky at the horizon almost exactly, which washes the distant sea white. Lower values pass the difference into the water, where it is absorbed, so the surface darkens by taking in more light rather than by light going missing.
caustica.options.rt.parallaxDepth.toolti: How far a material's height map may sink its surface, as a percent of the depth LabPBR authors (25% of a block at 100%). Only surfaces whose normal map carries a height field are affected. Set to 0% to turn parallax off entirely and compare, which is the quickest way to tell a parallax artifact from anything else on the surface.
caustica.options.rt.parallaxLayers.toolt: Ceiling on how many height samples one displaced texel may cost. The march works out how many it needs from how far the surface has to travel, so most views pay far less than this; the ceiling only bites on steep, deep relief, where a higher one resolves the step instead of coarsening it. Lower it if parallax costs more frame time than it is worth.
caustica.options.rt.entityParallax.toolt: Run the height-field parallax march on entities as well as on terrain. Entities only carry a height field when a resource pack gives them a normal map with an authored alpha, so with vanilla assets this changes nothing.
caustica.options.rt.textureEmission.tool: Honour the emissive channel a resource pack authors in its own specular map. It is the only light a material's textures can add by themselves; switching it off leaves the rest of the material intact and is the way to tell whether a glow belongs to the texture or to the block.
caustica.options.rt.blockEmission.toolti: Honour light emitted by the block itself rather than by its texture: glowing block states such as glowstone, lava, torches and the like. Light already published to the emitter list keeps lighting the room until that section is rebuilt, so give it a moment after switching.
caustica.options.rt.subsurface.tooltip: Honour the subsurface scattering a material's LabPBR map asks for, which lets light bleed a short distance through waxy and organic surfaces. Switched off, those surfaces keep their colour and shading but stop scattering.
caustica.options.rt.porosity.tooltip: Honour the porosity a material's LabPBR map asks for, which is what lets a wet surface absorb water and darken. Switched off, Surface Wetness still adds its sheen but nothing drinks it, which separates a wet world from a porous material.
caustica.options.rt.wetness.tooltip: How much water the world has, against the porosity each material's own LabPBR map was authored with. At 0% everything is dry and porous surfaces look exactly as authored; at 100% a porous surface darkens and turns reflective as far as its map allows, so sand and wool react strongly while metal and glass stay unchanged. This sets how wet the world is, not which materials are porous.
caustica.options.rt.fog.tooltip: Analytic height fog integrated inside the path tracer: distant terrain fades into aerial perspective, foggy air picks up sunlight and god rays, and the sky darkens toward the horizon behind it. Off by default.
caustica.options.rt.fogDensity.tooltip: Fog extinction at the fog base, in 1/block — the same unit as the water medium's absorption. 2% puts the e-folding distance at 50 blocks; higher values close in until only tens of blocks stay visible inside the fog.
caustica.options.rt.fogHeight.tooltip: How many blocks of altitude the fog takes to fall to 1/e of its base density. Small values hug the ground; large ones fill valleys and climb hillsides.
caustica.options.rt.fogBaseY.tooltip: The world height where the fog's constant-density region ends and the exponential falloff begins, in absolute Y blocks.
caustica.options.rt.fogAnisotropy.toolti: How strongly the fog forward-scatters light. Positive values brighten fog in the direction of the sun or moon, which is what turns a flat bright haze into visible beams; 0% is isotropic.
caustica.options.rt.fogAlbedo.tooltip: The fraction of extinguished light the fog scatters back out rather than absorbs. Low values make fog darken with thickness like smoke; high values keep it bright and milky.
caustica.options.rt.fogAmbient.tooltip: Weight of the sky's own irradiance in the fog's lighting. This is what keeps night fog from going black — it fades with the sky instead of adding a constant glow.
caustica.options.rt.fogShadow.tooltip: Casts one shadow ray per pixel toward the sun or moon so terrain, trees and buildings cut real light shafts out of the fog. Off leaves the sun term unoccluded — uniform bright fog with no god rays.
caustica.options.rt.fogShadowFloor.toolt: The density fully-shadowed fog keeps. 0% hard-culls the fog from shadow — crisp shadow volumes but sterile edges; higher values keep more milk in sealed rooms and shaded valleys. 95% nearly disables the cull.
caustica.options.rt.fogMarch.tooltip: Steps the fog integral instead of using the closed form, so the fog gathers into wind-drifted billows and every sample casts its own sun shadow ray. Costly; with noise at 0% it converges to the same result as the analytic fog.
caustica.options.rt.fogNoise.tooltip: How strongly the fog density gathers into billows around its height profile. 0% reproduces the smooth analytic fog exactly; higher values make clumpy, uneven fog.
caustica.options.rt.fogWindSpeed.tooltip: How fast the billow field drifts, in blocks per second. The drift is a smooth translation of a world-anchored field, so shapes move steadily instead of boiling per frame.
caustica.options.rt.fogWindAngle.tooltip: The compass direction the billow field drifts toward. 0° blows toward +X (east).
caustica.options.rt.fogMarchSteps.toolti: March samples per path segment. More steps resolve the billows and light shafts more exactly but cost proportionally more; 16 is balanced, 64 is the convergence reference.
caustica.options.rt.fogJitter.tooltip: Scatters each march sample inside its step with a stable blue-noise pattern. 0% bands visibly at step edges; 100% dithers them into a grain the denoiser resolves into soft edges.
caustica.options.rt.cloudCoverage.toolti: How much of the sky the cloud layer claims. 0% is an empty sky; 100% washes most of the dome overcast. The layer is a flat sheet: it renders in the sky, casts the cloud shadows below, and dims the fog's sun shafts — all from one field.
caustica.options.rt.cloudPatchiness.tool: How strongly the clouds gather into localized systems with clear sky between them. 0% spreads the streaks uniformly over the whole dome; 100% breaks them into distinct cloud fields with real gaps. Fades out near full coverage, so 100% coverage still delivers a solid overcast.
caustica.options.rt.cloudAltitude.toolti: World height of the cloud plane, in blocks.
caustica.options.rt.cloudThickness.toolt: The slab depth the cloud's optical depth scales with: thicker clouds read denser and cast darker shadows, especially toward the horizon.
caustica.options.rt.cloudDensity.tooltip: Density multiplier on the cloud's optical depth — effectively the shadow strength. 0% leaves a thin bright veil with no shadow; 100% casts full storm-shadow darkness under thick patches.
caustica.options.rt.cloudWindSpeed.toolt: How fast the cloud field drifts, in blocks per second. The drift is a smooth translate of a world-anchored field — clouds move, they do not boil.
caustica.options.rt.cloudWindAngle.toolt: Compass direction the cloud field drifts toward. 0° blows toward +X (east).
caustica.options.rt.cloudFadeDistance.to: Distance in blocks where the cloud sheet fully dissipates: nothing renders past it, and the fade begins at 60% of this range. Cloud shadows keep working beyond it — the layer still exists overhead.
caustica.options.rt.cloudVolumetric.tool: Walk the cloud slab instead of crossing it once: real vertical structure, parallax as the camera moves, and a lit crown over a dark underbelly. Pays a step budget per primary-ray pixel; reflections and bounces keep the cheap mean extinction, so what they see is dimmed but not re-lit.
caustica.options.rt.cloudSteps.tooltip: Steps the volumetric tier walks across the slab per pixel. Cost is linear in this; the dithering the denoiser has to resolve is inversely so. Below the floor the slab’s rims alias visibly, above ~48 more samples stop changing the image.
caustica.options.rt.cloudType.tooltip: Vertical profile of the slab. 0% is a flat stratus board; 100% a rounded cumulus billow that thins at base and crown. Both carry the same column depth, so this changes the shape the light falls on, not how much cloud is overhead.
caustica.options.rt.cloudRainBoost.toolt: How much rain and thunder thicken the deck, on top of the coverage and density above. Rain lifts the coverage toward solid overcast and multiplies the density, so shadows go storm-dark; thunder adds a third again. 0% holds the sky to the sliders whatever the weather.
caustica.options.rt.volumeQuality.toolti: Sets the whole volumetric system at once and WRITES the settings below, so what the other controls show is what the frame is doing. Off clears every one of them and renders the world exactly as it did before the system existed; each tier above it adds one effect: Low the clouds, Medium the volumetric deck, High the fog layer, Ultra the marched fog. The tier name is what was last selected, not a reading of the other controls: adjust one of them by hand and the name stays where it was.
caustica.options.rt.cloud.tooltip: A flat cloud layer over the world: the sheet in the sky, plus cloud shadows on terrain, fog and water. Renders only where the sky lights the world; off keeps the sky exactly as before.
caustica.options.rt.fogRainBoost.tooltip: How strongly rain thickens the fog: density scales by 100% + boost × rain level, on top of the day curve rather than replacing it. 0% keeps the fog weather-blind.
caustica.options.rt.waterTurbidity.toolt: The fraction of the light water extinguishes that it re-scatters instead of absorbing. This is what underwater sun beams are made of: 0% keeps the previous pure-absorption look, higher values brighten the water body and let shafts read inside it. The scattering keeps the water's tint, so a blue ocean scatters blue.
caustica.options.rt.waterSpray.tooltip: A thin band of mist hugging the water surface, densest over agitated wave crests. Rides the marched fog integrator, so volumetric fog with its march tier must be on; 0% keeps it off. Rain thickens it on top of this base.
caustica.options.rt.waterOpacity.tooltip: How strongly water absorbs light as a percent of the default look (100%). Lower values make water clearer so you can see the bottom; higher values make it murkier and darker. 0% removes absorption entirely.
caustica.options.rt.hdr.tooltip: Recreate the swapchain for HDR (ST.2084/PQ) or native SDR output. Applied at the next frame boundary.
caustica.options.rt.hdrUiBrightness.tool: Absolute brightness (in nits) assigned to SDR-authored UI on an HDR display.
caustica.options.rt.hdrPeak.tooltip: Absolute brightness (in nits) highlights roll off toward. Set to your display's peak HDR brightness.
caustica.options.rt.dlssQuality.tooltip: DLSS Ray Reconstruction quality mode. Lower-quality modes render fewer pixels and upscale more aggressively for higher framerates; higher-quality modes render more pixels for a sharper image. Only affects the image when DLSS Ray Reconstruction is enabled.
caustica.options.rt.debugView.tooltip: Inspect ray-tracing buffers and exposure diagnostics after the normal frame has rendered.
caustica.setting.enabled.tooltip: Trace the scene with hardware ray tracing instead of the built-in rasterizer.
caustica.setting.worker-threads.tooltip: Background threads that build and upload terrain acceleration structures. More loads terrain faster but takes more CPU time. Applied at startup, so it needs a game restart.
caustica.setting.omm.tooltip: Precompute per-triangle opacity so empty space inside cutout and translucent blocks is skipped during traversal. Needs a game restart.
caustica.setting.ommSubdivision.tooltip: Resolution of the opacity micromap. Higher discards empty space more precisely but costs more to build. Needs a game restart.
caustica.setting.ommStats.tooltip: Log how cutout triangles were classified into fully opaque, fully transparent and mixed, at most once every five seconds while terrain is being built.
caustica.setting.asyncDispatch.tooltip: How many terrain sections are submitted for building in one render pass. Higher loads terrain faster but uses more CPU and GPU time.
caustica.setting.completionResults.toolt: How many finished terrain builds are collected in one render pass. Higher commits terrain sooner but uses more time per pass.
caustica.setting.maxInflight.tooltip: How many terrain sections may be building at the same time.
caustica.setting.sectionTableCapacity.to: Starting size of the table that holds one acceleration structure per terrain section.
caustica.setting.rebaseDistance.tooltip: Distance, in blocks, after which terrain coordinates are re-anchored around the camera so float precision stays fine far from the origin.
caustica.setting.blasCompaction.tooltip: Shrink rebuilt terrain acceleration structures after building them.
caustica.setting.minFillRatio.tooltip: How much of a block a glowing block has to fill before it is treated as an area emitter rather than a point light.
caustica.setting.lightTemporalReuse.tool: Carry each pixel's chosen emitter light forward from the previous frame and keep averaging it, instead of re-picking from scratch every frame. Turn off to compare the two directly at one spot.
caustica.setting.lightTemporalHistory.to: How many effective samples a pixel's emitter choice may accumulate before it stops admitting older frames. Lower keeps more per-frame randomness, which the upscaler averages instead of the reservoir; higher converges the brightness but freezes which emitter the pixel is lit by.
caustica.setting.lightStats.tooltip: Log the size of the ray-traced emitter hierarchy — how many emitters, section slots and grid spans it holds, how much memory that takes, and how many emitter indices survive each rebuild — every time it is rebuilt.
caustica.setting.lightDump.tooltip: Log one line per ray-traced emitter near the player each time the hierarchy is rebuilt, with its world position, area and emitted light, followed by a count.
caustica.setting.lightDumpRadius.tooltip: How far around the player, in blocks, the emitter dump reaches.
caustica.setting.nameTags.tooltip: Draw entity name tags inside the traced scene instead of over it.
caustica.setting.entityRefit.tooltip: Update a moving entity's acceleration structure in place instead of rebuilding it.
caustica.setting.maxOrdinary.tooltip: Upper bound on how many ordinary entities are captured into the traced scene. Needs a game restart.
caustica.setting.maxBlockEntities.toolti: Upper bound on how many block entities, such as signs and chests, are captured into the traced scene. Needs a game restart.
caustica.setting.beViewChunks.tooltip: How many chunks around the camera are searched for block entities to capture.
caustica.setting.beBuilds.tooltip: How many block entity renderers are captured in one frame. Higher fills the scene sooner but costs more per frame.
caustica.setting.maxEntityTextures.toolt: How many distinct entity textures are held open at once. Needs a game restart.
caustica.setting.entityPbr.tooltip: Read LabPBR material maps for entities so they can be rough, metallic, or emissive. Needs a game restart.
caustica.setting.captureParity.tooltip: Debug only: capture every entity model twice and require the two results to match exactly. Halves entity capture speed.
caustica.setting.maxParticles.tooltip: Upper bound on how many particles are captured into the traced scene. Needs a game restart.
caustica.setting.blockOutline.tooltip: Draw the targeted-block outline inside the traced scene instead of over it.
caustica.setting.exposureKey.tooltip: The scene brightness auto exposure treats as middle grey. Raising it brightens everything the meter sees; it does not change how much the meter compensates for scene range.
caustica.setting.adaptDarken.tooltip: Seconds auto exposure takes to adjust when the scene gets darker, such as walking into a cave.
caustica.setting.adaptBrighten.tooltip: Seconds auto exposure takes to adjust when the scene gets brighter, such as stepping back outside.
caustica.setting.lowPercentile.tooltip: The lower edge of the measured luminance range that auto exposure keeps.
caustica.setting.highPercentile.tooltip: The upper edge of the measured luminance range that auto exposure keeps.
caustica.setting.exposureStride.tooltip: How many pixels are skipped when sampling the frame for exposure. Higher meters faster and less accurately.
caustica.setting.centerSigma.tooltip: How wide the region at the middle of the screen is that counts more heavily toward exposure.
caustica.setting.centerFloor.tooltip: How much weight the rest of the screen keeps next to the centre region.
caustica.setting.skyWeightCap.tooltip: Limits how much open sky can pull on exposure, so looking at the horizon does not darken the ground.
caustica.setting.emissiveWeightCap.toolt: Limits how much glowing blocks can pull on exposure, so a torch in view does not darken the room.
caustica.setting.preExposure.tooltip: Store the traced image at the previous frame's exposure scale and divide it back out when displaying, so values stay near middle grey instead of spanning the full photometric range. Cancels exactly, so toggling it should not change the image; it exists to check that, and as an escape hatch if the upscaler proves sensitive to its history scale.
caustica.setting.dlssRr.tooltip: Denoise the traced image with NVIDIA Ray Reconstruction instead of presenting it directly. Requires supported hardware and drivers.
caustica.setting.dlssPreset.tooltip: 0 lets the Ray Reconstruction library choose its own default for the selected quality mode. Leave at 0 unless diagnosing upscaling behaviour.
caustica.setting.frameGeneration.tooltip: Generate additional displayed frames between traced ones. Requires supported hardware and drivers.
caustica.setting.multiFrameCount.tooltip: 1 displays 2 frames per traced frame, 2 displays 3, and so on.
caustica.setting.reflex.tooltip: Reduce click-to-photon latency through the low-latency Vulkan interface. Requires supported hardware.
caustica.setting.reflexBoost.tooltip: Raise GPU clocks while frames are being rendered.
caustica.setting.reflexInterval.tooltip: Pace frames to at most one per this many microseconds. 0 leaves the rate uncontrolled.
caustica.setting.jitterSignX.tooltip: Sign applied to the horizontal part of the sub-pixel jitter, both as reported to the upscaler and as applied to primary rays. The default follows the validated DLSS convention for Vulkan's flipped clip space. Change only when diagnosing upscaling artefacts.
caustica.setting.jitterSignY.tooltip: Sign applied to the vertical part of the sub-pixel jitter, both as reported to the upscaler and as applied to primary rays. The default follows the validated DLSS convention for Vulkan's flipped clip space. Change only when diagnosing upscaling artefacts.
caustica.setting.frameStats.tooltip: Write per-frame ray-tracing counters to rt-frame-stats/frame.csv and log a line when a frame hitches.
caustica.setting.exr.tooltip: Save an ACEScg EXR beside the normal F2 PNG while ray tracing is active.
caustica.options.rt.screenshot.exrUnavai: No ray-traced frame available for a residual-exposure EXR
caustica.setting.heavyDiagnostics.toolti: Enable vendor Vulkan diagnostics and a full crash dump on device loss. Roughly ten times slower acceleration structure builds and a measurable framerate cost, so turn on only while chasing a live crash.
